title: Delivery telemetry ledger record (v1)
description: One record per delivery cycle (issue, pr). A reopened issue that ships more than once legitimately produces one record per shipped PR — and so does an issue that ships one or more SLICES while deliberately remaining OPEN (closed_at null, issue #3550) — retro aggregation by issue treats such multi-cycle issues as multiple deliveries, and slice records as a class of their own rather than as completed issues. Authoritative data only: every field is an observed event (GitHub timestamp/label or a supplied run counter) or arithmetic over authoritative timestamps. No value is inferred, estimated, or guessed.

allOf.$comment: issue #3448: the gate <-> gate_runs coupling, encoded so a STANDARD Draft 2020-12 validator enforces it and not only delivery-telemetry.py. gate 'not-run' means no full gate of record ran, so the only coherent run count is 0; and 0 runs cannot have produced a pass/fail outcome. delivery-telemetry.py's _validate_gate_coupling enforces the same rule for this repo's minimal validator, which ignores if/then — the two are the same fact written for two audiences, so change them together.

schema.description: Record schema version. It tracks the RECORD SHAPE as defined by THIS COMMITTED FILE, which is versioned in git and widens COMPATIBLY IN PLACE — a widening does not bump it. Established by precedent, not preference: #2088 added the optional roborev_blockers/roborev_nits, #2667 added nudges/orphan_minutes, #3448 widened the gate enum with 'not-run', and #3550 made closed_at nullable — four widenings, all under schema 1. Each makes a new record invalid against the OLDER TEXT of this file, and that is accepted: the ledger and its only consumer (scripts/delivery-telemetry.py) are committed together, so the schema a record is read with is always the one in the same checkout. Bumping for closed_at alone would be inconsistent with the three prior widenings and would fork retro's aggregation for no reader that exists. A version bump is for a BREAKING change — a removed/renamed field, or a narrowed type — which none of the above is.

pr.description: GitHub PR number that DELIVERED this cycle. Usually the PR that closed the issue, but not always: a SLICE record (closed_at null, issue #3550) is a PR that shipped part of an issue which deliberately stays open, so it closed nothing.

routing.description: design = OpenSpec change; oracle = parity/repro bug.

created_at.description: GitHub issue createdAt (authoritative). CANONICAL SUBSET (issue #3550): the value must additionally match `pattern` — YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[.frac] followed by Z or +hh:mm, UPPERCASE. This is deliberately NARROWER than RFC-3339, which also permits lowercase 't'/'z' and a leap second (23:59:60): every timestamp in this ledger originates from `gh`, which always emits the uppercase canonical form, and `datetime.fromisoformat` cannot parse a leap second at all. The subset is stated HERE as a `pattern` rather than left implicit in the tool, because `format` is annotation-only for a standard Draft 2020-12 validator — so without it the published schema would accept spellings delivery-telemetry.py's `_is_rfc3339` rejects, and `lint` could refuse a record the schema allows. Same fact for two audiences: change the pattern and `_is_rfc3339` together.

closed_at.description: GitHub issue closedAt (authoritative), NULLABLE (issue #3550). The KEY is always required; its VALUE carries the record's kind, which is therefore a DEFINITION, not an inference: null <=> this record is a SLICE delivery — a merged PR shipping part of an issue that was DELIBERATELY OPEN when that PR merged (the shape the lead ruled correct on #3393); a non-null date-time <=> a COMPLETED-ISSUE delivery, and is then the issue's own closedAt. The slice assertion is about DELIVERY TIME, which the issue's CURRENT state cannot decide — GitHub records an auto-close AFTER the merge, so an ordinary completed delivery and a late-stamped slice have indistinguishable timestamps. delivery-telemetry.py therefore REFUSES --slice for a currently-CLOSED issue, for one open only because it was REOPENED (stateReason REOPENED — its closed_at is null now, which does not show it was open then, so an ordinary completed delivery would be mislabeled a slice), and during GitHub's post-merge AUTO-CLOSE PROPAGATION window, where an ordinary completed delivery presents identically to a never-closed issue (closed_at null AND stateReason empty) and only the PR's own closingIssuesReferences distinguishes them — a slice pr closes NOTHING. The first two need the issue timeline replayed to mergedAt (issue #3559); the third resolves itself once GitHub records the close. Closing an issue to satisfy this tool is FORBIDDEN — a tool's data model must never decide whether a problem is recorded as solved. The kind selects cycle_time_s's basis (see cycle_time_s), and `retro` reports slice records as their own class rather than as completed issues. CANONICAL SUBSET (issue #3550): the value must additionally match `pattern` — YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[.frac] followed by Z or +hh:mm, UPPERCASE. This is deliberately NARROWER than RFC-3339, which also permits lowercase 't'/'z' and a leap second (23:59:60): every timestamp in this ledger originates from `gh`, which always emits the uppercase canonical form, and `datetime.fromisoformat` cannot parse a leap second at all. The subset is stated HERE as a `pattern` rather than left implicit in the tool, because `format` is annotation-only for a standard Draft 2020-12 validator — so without it the published schema would accept spellings delivery-telemetry.py's `_is_rfc3339` rejects, and `lint` could refuse a record the schema allows. Same fact for two audiences: change the pattern and `_is_rfc3339` together.

cycle_time_s.description: Delivery cycle time in seconds (arithmetic over authoritative timestamps). Its BASIS is selected by closed_at (issue #3550): for a completed-issue delivery (closed_at non-null) it is closed_at - created_at; for a SLICE delivery (closed_at null) it is merged_at - created_at, because the PR's mergedAt is the authoritative terminal timestamp of a slice and the issue's closedAt is not the cycle boundary at all. The basis is cross-checked by delivery-telemetry.py's _validate_cycle_time_basis over the WHOLE ledger (arithmetic is outside this schema's expressible keywords, so unlike the gate <-> gate_runs coupling it is NOT duplicated in an allOf).

claim_collisions.description: Run-observed: number of rejected claim pushes (a competing session won the race).

rebase_events.description: Run-observed: number of rebases / merge-conflict resolutions.

gate.description: Run-observed: final agent-gate.sh outcome. 'not-run' (issue #3448) means NO full gate of record ran for this delivery — the honest value when the count is zero, never a stand-in for an unobserved outcome. MUST be paired with gate_runs: 0 (not-run <=> 0, both directions) — enforced TWICE, deliberately: by this schema's own top-level allOf (if/then), so a standard Draft 2020-12 validator rejects an incoherent pair, AND by delivery-telemetry.py's _validate_gate_coupling, because this repo's minimal validator ignores if/then. Same fact for two audiences — change both together.

gate_runs.description: Run-observed: number of agent-gate.sh runs through (and including) the first PASS — runs stop at the first pass, so failed rounds = gate_runs-1 for a terminal pass and gate_runs for a terminal fail. Do not re-run the gate after a pass. 0 is legal ONLY with gate: 'not-run' (issue #3448): the coupling gate: not-run <=> gate_runs: 0 holds in BOTH directions, so a pass/fail with 0 runs and a not-run with >0 runs are each rejected — enforced TWICE, deliberately: by this schema's own top-level allOf (if/then), so a standard Draft 2020-12 validator rejects an incoherent pair, AND by delivery-telemetry.py's _validate_gate_coupling, because this repo's minimal validator ignores if/then. Same fact for two audiences — change both together.

roborev_findings.description: Run-observed: count of roborev findings raised.

roborev_blockers.description: Run-observed, OPTIONAL (issue #2088): count of BLOCKER-severity roborev findings — see docs/development/roborev-severity.md. Present only when the reviewer of record classified findings by severity; absence means severity was not observed (authoritative-only, never zero-filled). MUST appear together with roborev_nits (both-or-neither); when both are present, roborev_blockers + roborev_nits MUST equal roborev_findings — enforced by delivery-telemetry.py's cross-field check (outside this schema's minimal validator).

roborev_nits.description: Run-observed, OPTIONAL (issue #2088): count of NIT-severity roborev findings — see docs/development/roborev-severity.md. MUST appear together with roborev_blockers (both-or-neither); the sum constraint with roborev_findings is documented on roborev_blockers.

nudges.description: Run-observed, OPTIONAL (issue #2667): number of manual lead nudges required during the cycle to un-stall background work (an idle closer/worker prodded back into motion). Present only when observed; absence means not-observed, never zero (authoritative-only).

orphan_minutes.description: Run-observed, OPTIONAL (issue #2667): total minutes background work sat completed-but-unowned this cycle (Mode-3 orphaned-endgame exposure). Present only when observed; absence means not-observed, never zero (authoritative-only).
